staging/how-it-works.text:
How ZeroTacky Works

One site for the whole meet: the promoter builds it on a phone or laptop, athletes find and enter it here, volunteers join with a six-character code on the day, and everyone watches the same live scoreboard. Pick the track that fits you.

PROMOTERS
ATHLETES & SPECTATORS
VOLUNTEERS & JUDGES
FAQ
WHAT'S COMING
RUNNING A SHOW
Promoters

You set the meet up once, on your phone or a laptop. When you publish it, every judge, pit crew phone, and the public scoreboard see the same divisions, events, and scores, so nobody is working from a different copy.

1
Create an account and tick Promoter

Your account is what proves a meet is yours. Only you can change or delete it, and if you lose your phone you sign in on another one and everything is still there. There is nothing to write down or pass around between promoters.

Account
2
Build the meet

On My Meets, New Meet asks for a name and a date and opens the meet as eight tabs: details and rules (admin PIN, run order, tiebreaker, gym plates), divisions, stations, events, athletes, listing, registrations and meet day. The phone scorer has the same steps under Meet Setup if you would rather build it there. The first-show guide walks through every tab with pictures.

Set up your first show
3
List it and open entries

A new meet starts unlisted: it has a web page, but only people with the link can see it. On the Listing tab you tick Listed to put it in Find a Show, fill in the venue and entry fee, and decide whether athletes can register right now, join a waitlist, or only enter on the day. Building on the phone instead? Publish from the scorer while signed in and the meet lands under My Meets the same way.

My Meets
4
Approve registrations

When an athlete registers, their entry appears on your Registrations tab with the division they picked and their signed waiver. Accepting them adds them to the roster for that division. You can also decline, or leave them pending while you sort out numbers.

5
Hand out the join code on meet day

The Meet Day tab shows a six-character code. Anyone helping you enters it on Join a Meet and their phone is connected to your meet. Judges and anyone who needs to change the setup also type in the admin PIN from step 1. If the code gets out to people who should not have it, tap rotate and the old one stops working.

Join a Meet
6
Share the live scoreboard

Every published meet gets a web page with the standings, each event's results and who is up next. The link is on the Meet Day tab. Put it on a TV in the gym with the TV layout and send it to spectators, who can open it on any phone without signing in.

See a demo board
Setting up your first show, step by step

One meet from a blank screen to posted results, with a picture of every screen and what each change does on the public side.

COMPETING AND WATCHING
Athletes & Spectators

Find a show, keep an eye on it, register when entries open, then follow the scoring live on the day. Shows marked DEMO are made up so you can see what a listing and a scoreboard look like; they do not take entries.

1
Find a show

Search by name, division, status, state, implement, or federation. Each show page has the venue, the divisions and events, and whether registration is open.

Find a Show
2
Follow it

If you are signed in you can tap Follow on a show you are thinking about. It then appears under Following on your My Meets page so you can find it again without searching. Following does not enter you in anything and the promoter is not told.

Account
3
Register

Once entries are open, pick your division, give an emergency contact and your date of birth, and sign the waiver. You need to be 12 or older on the day of the meet. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian fills in their part of the form.

4
Track it on My Meets

Your entry starts as Pending approval until the promoter looks at it, then becomes Registered, Waitlisted, or Declined. After the meet it moves to Completed, so over time My Meets becomes a record of where you have competed.

My Meets
5
Watch live

The scoreboard page updates as judges enter scores. If you are at the venue you can also enter the join code on Join a Meet and see the Next Up list, including the weights and heights for each athlete, without being able to change anything.

Join a Meet
MEET-DAY CREW
Volunteers & Judges

You do not need an account. The promoter gives you a six-character code, you pick what you are doing that day, and the app opens already set up for your job.

1
Enter the join code

Open Join a Meet and type the code. The meet name comes back so you can check it is the right one.

Join a Meet
2
Pick your role

Athlete or Spectator shows the standings and who is up next, with nothing to tap by accident. Volunteer is for pit crew and shows the plate loading calculator. Judge and Promoter need the admin PIN from the promoter; you type it once and the phone remembers which role you chose.

3
Judges: score from the pad

Pick the event and the athletes come up in the right order. Enter reps, time, distance, the bar height reached or stone splits, depending on the event. Scores go to the scoreboard the moment the phone has signal.

4
Pit crew: load from Next Up

Next Up shows who is lifting, the weight they need, the plates to put on each side and any rack or pin height, so nobody is doing plate maths at the bar. The promoter decides whether you can change the bar weight or enter a custom load.

5
Lose signal? Keep going

The app keeps working with no signal. Anything you enter is held on the phone and sent as soon as it reconnects, so a dead spot in the gym does not cost you any scores.

COMMON QUESTIONS
FAQ
EVERYONE
Does it cost anything?
No. Finding shows, registering, running a meet, the live scoreboard and the gym directory are all free right now. If that changes for any part of it, the price will be on the page before you use it, and what is already free for athletes stays free.
Does it work without Wi-Fi?
Yes. Scoring happens on the phone and is held there until it can be sent. A judge can score a whole event with no signal, and the public scoreboard catches up when the phone reconnects.
Do I need to install an app?
No. Everything runs in the browser on any phone, tablet or laptop. Promoters and judges can add the scorer to the home screen so it opens like an app, but nothing is downloaded from a store. Open the scorer
I forgot my password.
On the sign-in form, enter your email and tap Forgot password. The email you get has a link that brings you back to the Account page to choose a new one. If you are already signed in, use Change password on the same page. Account
What happens to my data?
What you enter when you register goes to the promoter of that meet, and ZeroTacky keeps what it needs to run the service. Your email is never shown publicly. The Privacy Policy lists what is kept and for how long. Privacy Policy
ATHLETES AND SPECTATORS
Do I need an account to register for a show?
No. The registration form works without one. If you sign in first, the entry lands on your My Meets page so you can see when the promoter accepts it, and after the meet it stays there as part of your record. You need to be 12 or older on the day of the meet; under 18, a parent or guardian completes their part of the waiver. Find a Show
How do I watch a show live?
Open the show page and tap the live scoreboard link. It shows standings, each event and who is up next, and updates as judges score. No account, no code. If you are at the venue, the promoter can also give you the join code, which adds the Next Up list with each athlete's weights.
What shows up publicly about me?
Once the promoter accepts you, your name and division appear on the meet roster and the live scoreboard, the same as a printed start list. Your email, date of birth and emergency contact go to the promoter only. Nothing else is public unless you turn on your own athlete page.
How do I get my own athlete page?
On your Account page, pick a username and turn on Show my profile publicly. Your name, photo, roles, location, home gym, favorite lift, PRs and the social handles you added show at zerotacky.com/athletes/yourname and in the Athletes list. Turn it off any time and the page is gone. Athletes
PROMOTERS
What do I need to run a show on ZeroTacky?
An account with Promoter ticked, your phone or a laptop to set the meet up, and one phone per judge on the day. Nothing is installed and the gym does not need Wi-Fi. The first-show guide walks through the whole thing with pictures. Set up your first show
Join code or admin PIN: who gets which?
Two codes, two jobs. The six-character join code gets a phone into your meet; give it to everyone helping, and to athletes or spectators who want the Next Up list. The admin PIN lets a joined phone score and change the setup; give it to judges and your co-promoters only. Both are on the Meet Day tab.
Can other people help me run it?
Yes. Anyone with the join code and the admin PIN can judge or edit from their phone; several phones can score different stations at the same time and everything merges. The meet itself belongs to your account, so only you can list, unlist or delete it.
How do athletes get on the roster?
Two ways, and you can mix them. Open registration on the Listing tab and athletes register from the show page; each entry appears on your Registrations tab and you accept, decline or waitlist it. Or type athletes straight into the roster in Meet Setup, which is what most people do for a small show or for day-of entries.
Can I unlist or delete a meet?
Unlist any time from the Listing tab; the meet stays yours, it just leaves Find a Show. Delete from the Meet Day tab as long as the meet is not running or finished; if it already has athletes or results you type its name to confirm. Finished meets are kept so results stay available. My Meets
GYM OWNERS
My gym is in the directory. How do I claim it?
Open the gym's page and tap Claim this gym, then give your name, email and role at the gym. Sign in first and the approved listing attaches to your account straight away; otherwise we confirm by email. We check each claim against the gym's own site or contact address. Once approved, the listing is yours to edit from My Gym: equipment, day passes, drop-in hours, website and contact. Gym Directory
My gym is not listed. How do I add it?
Sign in, tick Gym owner on your Account page, and use Add my gym. It goes into a short review queue so the directory stays real gyms with real equipment, then appears under your account. Add my gym
NOT HERE YET
What's coming

Everything above is live today and free. These are the next pieces, in roughly the order we plan to build them.

Paid show registration

Promoters set an entry fee and athletes pay when they register, instead of settling up separately.

Day passes from the gym directory

Buy a drop-in pass for a listed gym from its page, so travelling athletes can train on the way to a show.

Trainer directory

Coaches who train in person or online get their own searchable list, built from the trainer flag on athlete profiles.

Show history on athlete pages

Meets you competed in, with placings, listed on your public page once the promoter marks the show complete.

Gyms and shows linked both ways

A show page points at its host gym, and a gym page lists the shows it has hosted.

How It Works
 PROMOTER GUIDE
Set up your first show

This walks one made-up meet, the Iron Harbor Classic, from a blank screen to meet day. Every screen below is the real one you will use, and each step says what it changes for athletes and spectators. Budget about half an hour the first time.

WHAT YOU NEED
A ZeroTacky account with Promoter ticked on the Account page. The meet belongs to that account, so it follows you from laptop to phone and only you can change it.
A laptop for the setup. Everything here also works from the phone scorer under Meet Setup, but the tabs are easier to read on a bigger screen.
On the day: one phone per judge and one for the pit crew. Volunteers do not need accounts; they join with a code you hand out in step 9.
1
Create the meet
2
Meet details and rules
3
Divisions
4
Stations and floor plan
5
Events
6
Athletes
7
List it and open entries
8
Approve registrations
9
Meet day codes and screens
10
The live scoreboard
1
MY MEETS, NEW MEET
Create the meet

Open My Meets and tap New Meet. It asks for the name, the competition date and an optional web address. The address (the slug) becomes zerotacky.com/shows/your-slug; leave it blank and one is made from the name.

Create & Open Meet saves the meet to your account and opens it as eight numbered tabs. The order of the tabs is the order you fill them in.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Nothing yet. A new meet starts unlisted, so it is not in Find a Show. Its page exists at the direct link, which is handy for checking your work before anyone else sees it.

My Meets
2
TAB 1, MEET
Meet details and rules

The admin PIN is four to six digits. Judges and anyone who needs to change the setup on meet day type it once on their phone, after the join code from step 9. Collar weight is per pair and is added to every bar load the pit crew calculator shows.

Athlete run order decides who lifts when. Reverse Overall Points is the usual choice: the leader goes last so the podium race builds. Reverse Previous Event looks only at the last event. Roster Order never reshuffles. The screen explains each one under the buttons.

The tiebreaker only matters when two athletes finish on the same points. Available Gym Plates tells the pit crew calculator what it is allowed to use; turn off anything the gym does not own.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The run order drives the Next Up list on the scoreboard and on volunteer phones. Plates and collars drive the loads the pit crew sees. None of this is shown to athletes directly.

3
TAB 2, DIVISIONS
Divisions

Add one division per weight class or experience group, named the way athletes expect to read them. Type a name and press Add; the arrows reorder them.

The order here is the order they appear everywhere else: the registration dropdown, the scoreboard and the show card. Edits sit in working memory until you press Save Changes in the banner at the bottom.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Division names show as chips on the show card in Find a Show, as the choices on the registration form and as the sections of the live scoreboard.

4
TAB 3, STATIONS
Stations and floor plan

A station is one set of implements running its own order. Divisions on the same station run back to back; two stations run at the same time in different parts of the gym.

A small meet is fine on one station. Most promoters decide this after sign-ups close, when they know how many athletes each division has. Rename the stations if the gym calls them something else. If one station runs the events in a different order from the rest, the arrows on its card set that order.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Each station gets an Up Now strip at the top of the scoreboard, so spectators can see who is lifting where. Next Up on the volunteer phones is per station.

5
TAB 4, EVENTS
Events

Add Event opens the form. Pick how it is scored (reps, max weight, time or distance, time or implements), set the time cap and lanes, then tell the loader how the implement works: load points is how many places plates go on, tare is what the empty implement weighs. Those two numbers are what make the pit crew plate maths right.

Under per-division weights, enter the target weight for each division. Add a callout title if the pit crew should see a note, for example the keg or the pin height. Save Event, then Save Changes.

Events run in the order listed. Use the arrows on the cards if the running order changes.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Implement names show as chips on the show card. The registration page lists every division with its target weight for each event, so athletes know what they are signing up to lift. The scoreboard gets one column per event.

6
TAB 5, ATHLETES
Athletes

There are two ways onto the roster. Athletes who register online land here when you accept them in step 8. Paper sign-ups and walk-ins you add yourself: Bulk Add takes one name per line into a division, Single Add takes one at a time.

Each athlete gets a lot number inside their division. That is the order for the first event, and the fallback order whenever two athletes are level.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Roster names appear on the live scoreboard as soon as the meet is listed, with a dash in every event column until scores come in. Add only athletes you expect to show up.

7
TAB 6, LISTING
List it and open entries

Tick Listed to put the meet in Find a Show. The three status dropdowns are the badges the public sees: competition status (upcoming, live, completed), registration status (open, waitlist, closed, day-of only) and results status.

Fill in the venue, the federation or format, the entry fee as you want it displayed, the deadline, an athlete cap and a contact. No money moves through the site; the fee line tells athletes how you want to be paid. Save Listing Settings writes it straight to the server.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

This tab is the public face of the show. The card in Find a Show, the show page and the top of the registration page are all built from it, and the capacity line counts accepted entries against your cap.

Find a Show
The card athletes see in Find a Show.
The show page at zerotacky.com/shows/your-slug.
8
TAB 7, REGISTRATIONS
Approve registrations

An athlete signs in or creates a free account on the form, picks a division, gives a name, email, emergency contact and date of birth, signs the waiver and submits. The entry is tied to their account, which is how it shows on their My Meets page. Under-18s are entered by a parent or guardian from the guardian's account.

Each entry shows up here as Pending with the division and the signed waiver. Accept adds the athlete to that division roster with the next lot number; Decline removes them. Emergency contacts and dates of birth are visible to you only.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The athlete sees Pending, then Registered or Declined, on their My Meets page. Accepted entries count toward the capacity line on the registration page.

What the athlete fills in.
What you see.
9
TAB 8, MEET DAY
Meet day codes and screens

The six-character join code is how volunteer phones attach to your meet. Print Both gives you two QR codes for the gym wall: one for judges and pit crew, one for the live scoreboard. Rotate the code if it gets out to people who should not have it; phones signed in to your account are unaffected.

Volunteers open Join a Meet, enter the code and pick a role. Athlete and Spectator are read-only. Pit crew get the loading calculator. Judge and Promoter also type the admin PIN from step 2.

The scorer link is for your own phone. The TV link is a full-width standings table for a laptop plugged into the gym TV.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The scoreboard link is public and needs no sign-in. Share it with spectators and put the TV layout on a screen in the gym.

Join a Meet
What a volunteer sees after scanning the join QR.
10
ZEROTACKY.COM/M/YOUR-SLUG
The live scoreboard

As judges score, the board updates on every phone and TV that has it open. Each division is its own table, with one column per event and the total on the right. The strips at the top show who is up on each station, and the chips filter to one division.

When the last event is in, go back to the Listing tab and set competition status to Completed and results to Final. The show moves to Completed on every athlete's My Meets page and the standings stay up as the record of the day.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

This is the page spectators share. It works on any phone with no app and no account, and it keeps the final standings after the show.

See a demo board
After the show

Set the statuses to Completed and Final on the Listing tab and the show becomes a record: the public page and scoreboard stay up, and it moves to Completed on every athlete's My Meets. A video walkthrough of this guide is coming after our first full show.

How ZeroTacky Works

One site for the whole meet: the promoter builds it on a phone or laptop, athletes find and enter it here, volunteers join with a six-character code on the day, and everyone watches the same live scoreboard. Pick the track that fits you.

PROMOTERS
ATHLETES & SPECTATORS
VOLUNTEERS & JUDGES
FAQ
WHAT'S COMING
RUNNING A SHOW
Promoters

You set the meet up once, on your phone or a laptop. When you publish it, every judge, pit crew phone, and the public scoreboard see the same divisions, events, and scores, so nobody is working from a different copy.

1
Create an account and tick Promoter

Your account is what proves a meet is yours. Only you can change or delete it, and if you lose your phone you sign in on another one and everything is still there. There is nothing to write down or pass around between promoters.

Account
2
Build the meet

On My Meets, New Meet asks for a name and a date and opens the meet as eight tabs: details and rules (admin PIN, run order, tiebreaker, gym plates), divisions, stations, events, athletes, listing, registrations and meet day. The phone scorer has the same steps under Meet Setup if you would rather build it there. The first-show guide walks through every tab with pictures.

Set up your first show
3
List it and open entries

A new meet starts unlisted: it has a web page, but only people with the link can see it. On the Listing tab you tick Listed to put it in Find a Show, fill in the venue and entry fee, and decide whether athletes can register right now, join a waitlist, or only enter on the day. Building on the phone instead? Publish from the scorer while signed in and the meet lands under My Meets the same way.

My Meets
4
Approve registrations

When an athlete registers, their entry appears on your Registrations tab with the division they picked and their signed waiver. Accepting them adds them to the roster for that division. You can also decline, or leave them pending while you sort out numbers.

5
Hand out the join code on meet day

The Meet Day tab shows a six-character code. Anyone helping you enters it on Join a Meet and their phone is connected to your meet. Judges and anyone who needs to change the setup also type in the admin PIN from step 1. If the code gets out to people who should not have it, tap rotate and the old one stops working.

Join a Meet
6
Share the live scoreboard

Every published meet gets a web page with the standings, each event's results and who is up next. The link is on the Meet Day tab. Put it on a TV in the gym with the TV layout and send it to spectators, who can open it on any phone without signing in.

See a demo board
Setting up your first show, step by step

One meet from a blank screen to posted results, with a picture of every screen and what each change does on the public side.

COMPETING AND WATCHING
Athletes & Spectators

Find a show, keep an eye on it, register when entries open, then follow the scoring live on the day. Shows marked DEMO are made up so you can see what a listing and a scoreboard look like; they do not take entries.

1
Find a show

Search by name, division, status, state, implement, or federation. Each show page has the venue, the divisions and events, and whether registration is open.

Find a Show
2
Follow it

If you are signed in you can tap Follow on a show you are thinking about. It then appears under Following on your My Meets page so you can find it again without searching. Following does not enter you in anything and the promoter is not told.

Account
3
Register

Once entries are open, sign in or create a free account on the form itself, then pick your division, give an emergency contact and your date of birth, and sign the waiver. You need to be 12 or older on the day of the meet. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian creates the account and fills in their part of the form.

4
Track it on My Meets

Your entry starts as Pending approval until the promoter looks at it, then becomes Registered, Waitlisted, or Declined. After the meet it moves to Completed, so over time My Meets becomes a record of where you have competed.

My Meets
5
Watch live

The scoreboard page updates as judges enter scores. If you are at the venue you can also enter the join code on Join a Meet and see the Next Up list, including the weights and heights for each athlete, without being able to change anything.

Join a Meet
MEET-DAY CREW
Volunteers & Judges

You do not need an account. The promoter gives you a six-character code, you pick what you are doing that day, and the app opens already set up for your job.

1
Enter the join code

Open Join a Meet and type the code. The meet name comes back so you can check it is the right one.

Join a Meet
2
Pick your role

Athlete or Spectator shows the standings and who is up next, with nothing to tap by accident. Volunteer is for pit crew and shows the plate loading calculator. Judge and Promoter need the admin PIN from the promoter; you type it once and the phone remembers which role you chose.

3
Judges: score from the pad

Pick the event and the athletes come up in the right order. Enter reps, time, distance, the bar height reached or stone splits, depending on the event. Scores go to the scoreboard the moment the phone has signal.

4
Pit crew: load from Next Up

Next Up shows who is lifting, the weight they need, the plates to put on each side and any rack or pin height, so nobody is doing plate maths at the bar. The promoter decides whether you can change the bar weight or enter a custom load.

5
Lose signal? Keep going

The app keeps working with no signal. Anything you enter is held on the phone and sent as soon as it reconnects, so a dead spot in the gym does not cost you any scores.

COMMON QUESTIONS
FAQ
EVERYONE
Does it cost anything?
No. Finding shows, registering, running a meet, the live scoreboard and the gym directory are all free right now. If that changes for any part of it, the price will be on the page before you use it, and what is already free for athletes stays free.
Does it work without Wi-Fi?
Yes. Scoring happens on the phone and is held there until it can be sent. A judge can score a whole event with no signal, and the public scoreboard catches up when the phone reconnects.
Do I need to install an app?
No. Everything runs in the browser on any phone, tablet or laptop. Promoters and judges can add the scorer to the home screen so it opens like an app, but nothing is downloaded from a store. Open the scorer
I forgot my password.
On the sign-in form, enter your email and tap Forgot password. The email you get has a link that brings you back to the Account page to choose a new one. If you are already signed in, use Change password on the same page. Account
What happens to my data?
What you enter when you register goes to the promoter of that meet, and ZeroTacky keeps what it needs to run the service. Your email is never shown publicly. The Privacy Policy lists what is kept and for how long. Privacy Policy
ATHLETES AND SPECTATORS
Do I need an account to register for a show?
Yes, a free one, and you can create it right on the registration form without leaving the page. The entry is tied to your account: it shows on My Meets so you can see when the promoter accepts it, and after the meet it stays there as part of your record. You need to be 12 or older on the day of the meet; under 18, a parent or guardian creates the account, registers you and completes their part of the waiver. Find a Show
How do I watch a show live?
Open the show page and tap the live scoreboard link. It shows standings, each event and who is up next, and updates as judges score. No account, no code. If you are at the venue, the promoter can also give you the join code, which adds the Next Up list with each athlete's weights.
What shows up publicly about me?
Once the promoter accepts you, your name and division appear on the meet roster and the live scoreboard, the same as a printed start list. Your email, date of birth and emergency contact go to the promoter only. Nothing else is public unless you turn on your own athlete page.
How do I get my own athlete page?
On your Account page, pick a username and turn on Show my profile publicly. Your name, photo, roles, location, home gym, favorite lift, PRs and the social handles you added show at zerotacky.com/athletes/yourname and in the Athletes list. Turn it off any time and the page is gone. Athletes
PROMOTERS
What do I need to run a show on ZeroTacky?
An account with Promoter ticked, your phone or a laptop to set the meet up, and one phone per judge on the day. Nothing is installed and the gym does not need Wi-Fi. The first-show guide walks through the whole thing with pictures. Set up your first show
Join code or admin PIN: who gets which?
Two codes, two jobs. The six-character join code gets a phone into your meet; give it to everyone helping, and to athletes or spectators who want the Next Up list. The admin PIN lets a joined phone score and change the setup; give it to judges and your co-promoters only. Both are on the Meet Day tab.
Can other people help me run it?
Yes. Anyone with the join code and the admin PIN can judge or edit from their phone; several phones can score different stations at the same time and everything merges. The meet itself belongs to your account, so only you can list, unlist or delete it.
How do athletes get on the roster?
Two ways, and you can mix them. Open registration on the Listing tab and athletes register from the show page; each entry appears on your Registrations tab and you accept, decline or waitlist it. Or type athletes straight into the roster in Meet Setup, which is what most people do for a small show or for day-of entries.
Can I unlist or delete a meet?
Unlist any time from the Listing tab; the meet stays yours, it just leaves Find a Show. Delete from the Meet Day tab as long as the meet is not running or finished; if it already has athletes or results you type its name to confirm. Finished meets are kept so results stay available. My Meets
GYM OWNERS
My gym is in the directory. How do I claim it?
Open the gym's page and tap Claim this gym, then give your name, email and role at the gym. Sign in first and the approved listing attaches to your account straight away; otherwise we confirm by email. We check each claim against the gym's own site or contact address. Once approved, the listing is yours to edit from My Gym: equipment, day passes, drop-in hours, website and contact. Gym Directory
My gym is not listed. How do I add it?
Sign in, tick Gym owner on your Account page, and use Add my gym. It goes into a short review queue so the directory stays real gyms with real equipment, then appears under your account. Add my gym
NOT HERE YET
What's coming

Everything above is live today and free. These are the next pieces, in roughly the order we plan to build them.

Paid show registration

Promoters set an entry fee and athletes pay when they register, instead of settling up separately.

Day passes from the gym directory

Buy a drop-in pass for a listed gym from its page, so travelling athletes can train on the way to a show.

Trainer directory

Coaches who train in person or online get their own searchable list, built from the trainer flag on athlete profiles.

Show history on athlete pages

Meets you competed in, with placings, listed on your public page once the promoter marks the show complete.

Gyms and shows linked both ways

A show page points at its host gym, and a gym page lists the shows it has hosted.

The first event on a station runs by lot number. The reverse methods take over once an earlier event on that station has results.

Reverse Overall Pts
Reverse Prev Event

Reverse Overall Pts: Lowest overall points lifts first and the current leader goes last. Athletes level on points go by lot number. Most promoters pick this so the podium race builds to the final attempt.

Reverse Prev Event: Only the last event counts. Whoever placed last in it goes first and its winner goes last, whatever the overall standings. Athletes tied in that event go lower overall points first, then by lot number.

Roster Order: Athletes go in lot order for every event, never reshuffled. Pick this when the order was published ahead of time.

OVERALL PODIUM TIEBREAKER

Used only when two athletes finish on the same total points.

Most Event Wins
Final Event Score

Most Event Wins: The athlete with more event wins places higher. If that is level too, more points in the final event wins. Still level after both: the athletes share the place.

Final Event Score: The athlete with more points in the final event places higher. If that is level too, more event wins. Still level after both: the athletes share the place.
